candidates.title: The on-chain step verifier cannot be regenerated from audited source: uarch-step.cpp uses TLB_NUM_SETS, which the pinned machine-solidity-step generator does not emit
candidates.component: machine-solidity-step v0.17.0-test1 generator and template, regenerated from audit/prt2 (src/uarch-step.cpp)
candidates.role: Referee verifier (the regenerated UArchStep.sol is what Dave's CartesiStateTransition deploys)
candidates.location: src/uarch-step.cpp:890 (executeECALL, WRITE_TLB: `set_index >= TLB_NUM_SETS || slot_index >= TLB_SET_SIZE`, added by afd5f9d, whose message says 'UArchStep.sol picks up the check when it is regenerated'); machine-solidity-step helper_scripts/generate_EmulatorConstants.lua (emits no TLB_NUM_SETS) and templates/EmulatorConstants.sol.template (hand-codes TLB_SLOT_LENGTH=32, TLB_SET_SIZE=256, no TLB_NUM_SETS); regenerated src/UArchStep.sol:1090 leaves `TLB_NUM_SETS` unqualified; bugs/harness/work/solidity-step/build-status.txt
candidates.description: R13 requires 'The uarch program, its pristine hash, and the verifier code that a deployment fixes on-chain must be reproducibly buildable from audited source.' The audited source pair (emulator audit/prt2 plus the pinned generator machine-solidity-step v0.17.0-test1) does not produce a verifier that compiles. The translator only qualifies identifiers it finds in EmulatorConstants.sol. generate_EmulatorConstants.lua emits the constants it knows from the Lua module, and the template hand-codes only TLB_SLOT_LENGTH and TLB_SET_SIZE. So the TLB_NUM_SETS that uarch-step.cpp now uses stays a bare identifier, and `forge build` fails with 'Undeclared identifier' (UArchStep.sol:1090). The emulator exports CM_TLB_NUM_SETS and cartesi.TLB_NUM_SETS (commit 2a57a03), but nothing on the generator side reads them. A deployer must therefore hand-edit the template (the harness's labelled workaround patches/01-tlb-num-sets.sh adds `uint64 constant TLB_NUM_SETS = 3;`) or deploy an older step. A hand edit means the deployed verifier no longer comes from audited source, and its value is checked against the emulator by nothing (the same holds for the hand-coded TLB_SET_SIZE and TLB_SLOT_LENGTH, which feed EmulatorCompat.writeTlbECALL's slot address). An older step implements another version: v0.16.0 and v0.17.0-test1 have marchid 22, pristine hash 0x558f... and lack the TLB check.
candidates.trigger: A deployer (or Dave's build, doc/Dockerfile.prt with PRT_MACHINE_STEP_DIR) regenerates machine-solidity-step against audit/prt2 following its README (generate-step generate-constants ... then forge build).
candidates.reachability: Deterministic. Every regeneration of the step from this branch with the pinned generator fails to compile. No input or guest is involved.
candidates.rating_steps: 1. Out of scope? No. It needs no excluded condition, and the referee verifier is in scope ('machine-solidity-step v0.17.0-test1, with its generated code and constants regenerated from audit/prt2 | Referee verifier'). 2. Role: referee verifier (and the emulator source that feeds it, honest operator). 3. High/Medium cases: it matches the High case 'A uarch program or verifier code fixed on-chain that cannot be reproducibly rebuilt, while what is deployed matches its audited source.' It violates R13: 'the verifier code that a deployment fixes on-chain must be reproducibly buildable from audited source.' 4. Critical would need a deployed verifier that diverges, for example a hand-patched TLB_NUM_SETS with the wrong value, or a deployer falling back to a verifier of another version. With the correct value 3, the patched variant passes replay 56/56, so no divergence is shown. 5. n/a. Claimed High. If a deployment instead ships a hand-edited constant that differs from the emulator's, that is an A6 violation the deployment introduces, which is out of scope unless the emulator's build is what makes the obligation fail (here it does, because the audited source does not build).
candidates.threat_to_goal: A6/R13 rely on every deployment's verifier being the deterministic output of the audited emulator source. Because the build fails, the deployer has two choices. One is to edit the generated code or template by hand, which puts unaudited constants into the referee verifier (TLB_NUM_SETS, plus the already hand-coded TLB_SET_SIZE and TLB_SLOT_LENGTH that select the shadow TLB slot address the WRITE_TLB ecall writes). The other is to deploy a step of another version. Either way verifiers and operators may implement different transition functions, and the pristine-hash check of the players does not cover UArchStep code (see the related candidate).
candidates.evidence: Read bugs/harness/work/solidity-step/build-status.txt ('pure regeneration: forge build FAILED ... Undeclared identifier ... src/UArchStep.sol:1090:30 set_index >= TLB_NUM_SETS'). Checked that regenerated/src/UArchStep.sol:1090 has the bare `TLB_NUM_SETS` while `slot_index >= EmulatorConstants.TLB_SET_SIZE` is qualified, that generate_EmulatorConstants.lua has no TLB_* line, and that the template hand-codes TLB_SLOT_LENGTH/TLB_SET_SIZE. git show afd5f9d says 'UArchStep.sol picks up the check when it is regenerated'.
candidates.test_idea: A test.sh that copies work/solidity-step/released, points EMULATOR_DIR at the repository, runs `make generate-step generate-reset generate-send-cmio-response generate-constants` and `forge build` (or only compiles src/UArchStep.sol with the regenerated EmulatorConstants.sol). It exits 1 when the build fails. As a second assertion, it checks that every EmulatorConstants value used by the generated code (including TLB_NUM_SETS, TLB_SET_SIZE, TLB_SLOT_LENGTH) equals the emulator's cartesi.* constant.

candidates.title: Deployment and startup version checks compare only the uarch pristine hash, which does not cover UArchStep, UArchReset, SendCmioResponse or CM_MARCHID
candidates.component: PRT recipes: doc/recipes/crisium.lua (player startup), doc/recipes/prt-deploy.lua (deployment), doc/recipes/prt-lua-bridge.md (documentation)
candidates.role: Support (player, deploy script). It stands in for the honest operator's version check (R13).
candidates.location: doc/recipes/crisium.lua:126-132 and doc/recipes/prt-deploy.lua:44-48 (compare only CartesiStateTransition.UARCH_PRISTINE_STATE_HASH() with cartesi.UARCH_PRISTINE_STATE_HASH); doc/recipes/prt-lua-bridge.md:193-196; uarch/Makefile (the uarch RAM image is built from interpret.cpp and the device sources only, not from uarch-step.cpp, uarch-reset-state.cpp or send-cmio-response.cpp); CartesiStateTransition.CM_MARCHID (published, never read by the recipes)
candidates.description: R13: 'The honest operator must be able to detect and refuse a mismatch between its build and a deployment. The check must refuse every pairing of its build with a deployment of another released version.' The recipes check the deployed verifier only through UARCH_PRISTINE_STATE_HASH. That hash covers the uarch RAM image, which is compiled from the main-processor interpreter, plus the pristine uarch registers. It does not cover the generated uarch instruction interpreter (uarch-step.cpp -> UArchStep.sol), the reset/revert logic (uarch-reset-state.cpp -> UArchReset.sol), input delivery (send-cmio-response.cpp -> SendCmioResponse.sol), the hand-written EmulatorCompat/AccessLogs, or CartesiStateTransition's counter-to-form map. All of these are part of the transition function per R13 ('The accesses each logged transition makes, and their order', 'The map from position to transition form'). The deployed verifier also publishes CM_MARCHID 'so a claimer can compare it with its own emulator before joining', but no recipe reads it. The manual (prt-lua-bridge.md) states 'A matching CM_MARCHID does not guarantee that, which is why each player compares the deployed verifier's pristine hash', which suggests the pristine hash is a full version check. This branch's own history gives a concrete case: afd5f9d changed only src/uarch-step.cpp (the WRITE_TLB index check, which changes which logs UArchStep accepts) and left the uarch RAM image, and so the pristine hash, unchanged. A verifier generated before and one generated after that commit pass the player's check identically. Also, this branch reports the same version string (0.23.0-test2) and mimpid (23) as the released emulator v0.23.0-test2 that machine-solidity-step v0.17.0-test1 pairs with, so marchid (22 vs 23) is the only machine-ID register that differs, and the recipes never compare it with the verifier.
candidates.trigger: A deployment whose CartesiStateTransition comes from a step build with the same uarch program but different step, reset or delivery code (for example a step generated from a neighbouring emulator revision, or a hand-edited template as in the first candidate). The player starts against it and plays.
candidates.reachability: Needs a deployment that pairs this build's pristine uarch with a verifier of another version. For the released components I examined (step v0.16.0 and v0.17.0-test1, both pristine 0x558f.../marchid 22, vs this build's 0x89ae.../marchid 23), the pristine check does refuse the pairing. So no released pairing is shown to slip through. The gap is structural and is demonstrated by unreleased revisions on this branch.
candidates.rating_steps: 1. Out of scope? A deployment that mixes versions violates A6, but section 8 keeps in scope cases where 'the emulator's own behavior is what makes the obligation fail'. R13 makes detecting the mismatch the honest operator's duty, so the missing check is not excused. 2. Role: support (AUDIT.md: 'The PRT player and bridge in doc/recipes ... Support'). It stands in for the honest operator's version check. 3. High/Medium: in the honest-operator role this matches 'A node that cannot detect a version mismatch, while every node in fact runs the deployment's version' (High). A defect shown only by a support component is capped: 'A defect that only a support component shows is Medium when it would rate High or Critical in the role the component stands in for'. Medium. 4. It would be Critical only if a released pairing passed the check and the versions diverged on a reachable state. Deciding fact: whether any released step build shares a pristine hash with a released emulator of a different transition function. None is known among v0.16.0, v0.17.0-test1 and v0.23.0-test2/audit/prt2. 5. If triage reads R13 as satisfied because every known released pairing is refused, this is Low (manual overstates the check). Claimed Medium.
candidates.threat_to_goal: If verifier and operator disagree on step, reset or delivery semantics, the honest operator's proof of a disputed transition may fail to verify (completeness failure), or the verifier may accept a transition the operator's transition function does not produce. The goal assumes A6. R13 asks the operator to detect a violation, and the recipe operator cannot detect this class.
candidates.evidence: Read crisium.lua and prt-deploy.lua: the only verifier comparison is UARCH_PRISTINE_STATE_HASH(). grep for marchid/CM_MARCHID in doc/recipes finds only the prose in prt-lua-bridge.md. uarch/Makefile builds uarch-ram.bin from interpret.cpp, htif/plic/clint address ranges and uarch runtime sources, not uarch-step.cpp. `git show afd5f9d --stat`: only src/uarch-step.cpp and a test changed. src/cm-version.h: CM_VERSION 0.23.0-test2, CM_MIMPID = 23. machine-solidity-step v0.17.0-test1 README: 'pairs machine-solidity-step v0.17.0-test1 with machine-emulator v0.23.0-test2' (marchid 22). Dave's pinned machine/step fb00a32 (v0.16.0) has src identical to v0.17.0-test1.
candidates.test_idea: Deploy (via bugs/harness/chain/deploy.sh) a CartesiStateTransition built from the regenerated step with one UArchStep change that leaves EmulatorConstants intact (for example the TLB check removed, as before afd5f9d), then run crisium.lua's startup checks (or a copy of its verifier check). The test asserts that startup refuses the deployment. It exits 1 when startup accepts it. A second assertion checks that the startup code reads CM_MARCHID() and compares it with cartesi.MARCHID.

candidates.title: The default PRT image builds Dave with its pinned step v0.16.0 (marchid 22, pristine 0x558f...), another version than this emulator, contrary to the manual
candidates.component: doc/Dockerfile.prt and doc/Makefile build-prt-image (PRT recipe image); doc/recipes/prt-lua-bridge.md
candidates.role: Support (recipe image and documentation). It stands in for the referee model deployment the recipes produce.
candidates.location: doc/Makefile:55-65 (PRT_MACHINE_STEP_DIR ?= empty 'keeps Dave's'); doc/Dockerfile.prt contracts stage (uses machine/step pinned by Dave v3.0.0-alpha.7 = fb00a32 'release v0.16.0' unless a step checkout is supplied); doc/recipes/prt-lua-bridge.md:193-194 ('The release's machine/step is generated against the emulator release this build uses, so their pristine uarch states match.')
candidates.description: With the default PRT_MACHINE_STEP_DIR, the image compiles Dave's CartesiStateTransition against Dave's pinned machine/step v0.16.0, whose EmulatorConstants has CM_MARCHID = 22 and UARCH_PRISTINE_STATE_HASH = 0x558f38f2.... This emulator (audit/prt2) has MARCHID 23 and pristine hash 0x89ae34ba.... Its uarch program and the generated step differ (TLB index check, halt/overflow status order). The recipe deployment therefore pairs verifier and operator of different versions, which A6 forbids ('Every verifier, the uarch program fixed on-chain, and every honest operator in a deployment implements the same state transition function'), and the manual's statement that their pristine states match is false for this branch. prt-deploy.lua's pristine-hash assertion catches it, so the documented default build fails loudly at deployment instead of settling anything. The non-default path, regenerating the step from this branch, fails to compile (first candidate). So no documented configuration builds a matching recipe deployment from audited source.
candidates.trigger: `make -C doc build-prt-image` with defaults, then the PRT demo (prt-demo.sh) deploys.
candidates.rating_steps: 1. Out of scope? The mixed-version deployment is an A6 violation by the deployment. Here the recipes themselves build that deployment, and section 3 says an implementation of the referee model 'stands in for that normative model' and defects in it are in scope. 2. Role: support (recipe image, documentation). 3. High/Medium: the mixed versions are detected by prt-deploy.lua ('emulator and Solidity pristine uarch hashes differ'), so no wrong settlement or proof follows, only a loud failure. A support defect that would not rate High/Critical in its stand-in role is 'Any other support defect is Low'. A contradiction between the manual and behavior 'takes the severity it would have if the manual were right'. If the manual were right, there would be no defect. 4. Not Critical: no reachable state settles wrongly. 5. Low. If triage considers that the recipe deployment stands in for a deployed referee whose verifier would be of another version without the deploy-time check, it would rate Medium (support cap). Claimed Low.
candidates.threat_to_goal: No direct threat while prt-deploy's pristine check stays in place. It shows that the version pairing of verifier and emulator is held together by documentation rather than by the build, which is what A6 needs to be robust.
candidates.evidence: bugs/harness/work/dave/released/machine/step: `git log -1` = fb00a32 'chore: release v0.16.0'; `git show HEAD:src/EmulatorConstants.sol` has CM_MARCHID 22 and pristine 0x558f38f2...; src identical to v0.17.0-test1 (diff -r empty). In-tree cartesi.UARCH_PRISTINE_STATE_HASH = 0x89ae34ba... (bugs/harness/work/uarch-rebuild/report.txt). doc/Makefile:55-56 'A machine-solidity-step checkout whose sources replace the ones Dave pins. Empty keeps Dave's.'
candidates.test_idea: A test.sh that reads Dave's pinned machine/step EmulatorConstants.sol (git show HEAD in work/dave/released/machine/step) and compares CM_MARCHID and UARCH_PRISTINE_STATE_HASH with cartesi.MARCHID and cartesi.UARCH_PRISTINE_STATE_HASH. It exits 1 when they differ, which is what the default PRT image deploys.

candidates.title: The uarch toolchain is not fully pinned (binutils, cross libc headers, live Debian archive), so the pristine uarch hash is not guaranteed to be reproducible
candidates.component: Dockerfile (toolchain stage) and uarch/Makefile (uarch program build)
candidates.role: Honest operator (uarch program) / referee verifier (its pristine hash is fixed on-chain)
candidates.location: Dockerfile:1-17 (BUILD_BASE=debian:trixie-20250811 by tag; apt-get update from the live archive; only gcc-riscv64-unknown-elf=14.2.0+19 and g++-14-riscv64-linux-gnu=14.2.0-19cross1 are pinned); uarch/Makefile:1-29 (LD/OBJCOPY = riscv64-unknown-elf-ld/objcopy from binutils-riscv64-unknown-elf; headers -I/usr/riscv64-linux-gnu/include from libc6-dev-riscv64-cross)
candidates.description: The uarch RAM image whose hash every deployment fixes on-chain (UARCH_PRISTINE_STATE_HASH) is produced by the toolchain image. The image pins only the two compiler packages. The assembler/linker/objcopy (binutils-riscv64-unknown-elf, installed 2.44-3+7+b1), the C library headers the uarch includes (libc6-dev-riscv64-cross 2.41-11cross1, linux-libc-dev-riscv64-cross 6.12.38-1cross1) and the rest float with whatever the live trixie archive serves at build time. The base image is referenced by tag, not digest. A Debian point release can change any of them, which can change uarch-ram.bin and the pristine hash. Or it can remove the two pinned compiler versions from the live archive, after which the Dockerfile no longer builds at all. R13: 'The uarch program, its pristine hash, and the verifier code that a deployment fixes on-chain must be reproducibly buildable from audited source.'
candidates.trigger: Anyone (a deployer, auditor or operator) rebuilds the uarch from the audited tag after the Debian archive has moved.
candidates.reachability: Time-dependent. On 2026-11-14 the harness rebuild still matches (0x89ae...). I could not query the current archive from this sandbox (the proxy returns 405 for plain-HTTP apt).
candidates.rating_steps: 1. Out of scope? No. 2. Role: the uarch program is honest operator, and its hash is fixed by the referee verifier. 3. High/Medium: the listed High case is 'A uarch program or verifier code fixed on-chain that cannot be reproducibly rebuilt, while what is deployed matches its audited source.' Today it can be rebuilt, so this only fits if R13's 'reproducibly buildable' is read as requiring a build whose inputs are pinned. 4. Not Critical: what is deployed matches its source. 5. Otherwise Low (build hygiene). Deciding fact: whether a floating package version in the current trixie archive produces a different uarch-ram.bin, or whether the pinned compiler versions are still installable. Claimed Low, with High under the stricter reading.
candidates.threat_to_goal: Weakens R13's reproducibility guarantee for the on-chain uarch hash. Independent parties may be unable to confirm that a deployed UARCH_PRISTINE_STATE_HASH corresponds to audited source, so a mismatched uarch program could go undetected by rebuild.
candidates.evidence: `docker run --entrypoint dpkg cartesi/machine-emulator:toolchain -l`: binutils-riscv64-unknown-elf 2.44-3+7+b1, binutils-riscv64-linux-gnu 2.44-3, libc6-dev-riscv64-cross 2.41-11cross1, linux-libc-dev-riscv64-cross 6.12.38-1cross1 (unpinned). Also bugs/harness/README.md section 4 ('binutils-riscv64-unknown-elf 2.44-3+7+b1 is NOT pinned by the Dockerfile'). An apt-cache policy attempt from debian:trixie-20250811 failed (405 from the proxy).
candidates.test_idea: A test.sh that parses the Dockerfile's toolchain apt-get line and fails (exit 1) unless every package that contributes to uarch-ram.bin (gcc-riscv64-unknown-elf, binutils-riscv64-unknown-elf, g++-14-riscv64-linux-gnu, libc6-dev-riscv64-cross, libstdc++-14-dev-riscv64-cross, linux-libc-dev-riscv64-cross) has an exact version and the base image is pinned by digest or a snapshot.debian.org source is used. Alternatively, a rebuild from snapshot.debian.org at a later date compared against uarch/uarch-pristine-hash.c.

Also CartesiStateTransition's masks (LOG2_INPUT_WINDOW_SPAN 68, epoch span 92, UARCH_CYCLE_MASK) vs prt-ethereum.lua's hard-coded 92/68/48/20 and prt.lua's split/combine helpers. Input Merkle root (LibMath.ceilLog2, max 5) vs send_cmio_response's write size. Revert-root-hash leaf encoding and AccessLogs proof encoding vs prt-ethereum append_log. EmulatorCompat.writeTlbECALL vs the C++ write_unverified_tlb/replay slot hash. isYieldedManualWith in C++ and Solidity.
